name: Four-Week Strength for Running Calibration
description:
Four-week strength-training bundle built around daily running, the patched running calibration block, and the running support layer. Upper body maintains/improves physique; lower body is runner-centric, low-volume force production and durability rather than bodybuilding leg volume.

Companion bundles: four-week-running-calibration-patched (training_priority): Running calibration remains the priority. Strength should not contaminate HR/RPE calibration data. four-week-running-support-calibration (coordinate_load): Do not stack duplicate calf, soleus, hamstring, adductor, and core work if support cards are also active.

Program intent: upper-body physique maintenance plus runner-centric lower-body strength.

Default weekly structure: Push A / Lower A / Pull A / Push B / Lower B / Long-run no lift / Pull B.

Week 3 exception: During optional LTHR-test week, remove Lower B and make post-test upper lifting optional/light..

Progression model: Double progression: add reps inside the target range before adding load. Deload in Week 4..

Readiness gate: Run mechanics feel normal; No tendon pain above mild background noise; No unusual HR/RPE drift from prior day; No shoulder/elbow pain before pressing or pulling; No calf/Achilles/hamstring/adductor soreness before lower sessions.

Reduce if: Easy runs start feeling weird or heavy for more than 2 days; Calves/Achilles or hamstrings feel reactive; LTHR test is completed in Week 3; Sleep/fueling is poor; Upper joints feel irritated from pressing/curls.

routine_specs.name: Four-Week Strength for Running Calibration
routine_specs.notes: Designed to coexist with daily running. Week 3 deliberately reduces lower-body strength around the optional LTHR diagnostic test. Week 4 deloads. Coordinate with the support bundle to avoid duplicate lower-leg and hamstring/adductor work. The priority session goes first. For this block, run first; lift later whenever possible. Aim for 6+ hours between run and lift; 3-4 hours minimum for upper-only sessions. Leg work should make you stronger and more durable, not sore. No leg compounds to failure. Upper body can train closer to hypertrophy volume, but avoid elbow/shoulder irritation. Push days finish with triceps; pull days finish with biceps. Avoid turning every day into an arm day.
